title.zh: 卷八十二上 方術列傳
title.raw: 卷八十二上 方術列傳 Volume 82a: Biographies of Alchemists 1

sentences.zh: 仲尼稱《易》有君子之道四焉，曰「卜筮者尚其占」。

translations.literal: Confucius said that the Changes has four aspects of the way of the superior man, and among them he said, 'Those who divine by tortoise shell and milfoil esteem its prognostications.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius held that the Book of Changes embodies four paths fit for a gentleman, one of which is that those who practice tortoise and yarrow divination prize the oracle's verdict.

sentences.zh: 佔也者，先王所以定禍福，決嫌疑，幽贊於神明，遂知來物者也。

translations.literal: As for divination, it is what the former kings used to settle blessing and calamity, resolve what is doubtful, secretly assist the spirits and bright powers, and thereby know what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: Divination was how the ancient kings fixed fortune against misfortune, cut through uncertainty, drew hidden aid from the gods, and so discerned what lay ahead.

sentences.zh: 若夫陰陽推步之學，往往見於墳記矣。

translations.literal: As for the learning of yin and yang and calendrical reckoning, it is often seen already in old tomb inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: The yin-yang arts and astronomical computation already turn up again and again in those old grave records.

sentences.zh: 然神經怪牒、玉策金繩，關扃於明靈之府、封縢於瑤壇之上者，靡得而窺也。

translations.literal: Yet spirit scriptures and strange documents, jade tablets and golden cords, barred and bolted in the halls of the luminous spirits, sealed with vermilion lacquer upon the jade altar—none may spy them.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit texts and marvel registers, the jade slips bound with golden cord, locked away in the courts of the numinous and sealed on high altars, remain beyond anyone's sight.

sentences.zh: 至乃《河》、《洛》之文，龜龍之圖，箕子之術，師曠之書，緯候之部，鈐決之符，皆所以探抽冥賾、參驗人區，時有可聞者焉。

translations.literal: As for the writings of the Yellow River and the Luo, the charts of the tortoise and dragon, the arts of Jizi, the books of Shi Kuang, the categories of weft prognostications, and the tally-slips of secret decisions—all are means to plumb the dark profundities and cross-check the human realm, and from time to time something of them may be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Then there are the River and Luo documents, the tortoise-and-dragon diagrams, Jizi's methods, Shi Kuang's writings, apocryphal weft-books, and talismanic slips—all tools to sound the hidden depths and test them against the human world, and occasionally something credible surfaces.

sentences.zh: 其流又有風角、遁甲、七政、元氣、六日七分、逢佔、日者、挺專、須臾、孤虛之術，乃望雲省氣，推處祥妖，時亦有以效於事也。

translations.literal: In its wake there are further such arts as wind-angle, hidden stems, the seven luminaries, primordial qi, six days and seven parts, chance divination, day-masters, the bamboo slip method, momentary reckoning, and orphan-and-void calculations—by which men scan the clouds and read vapors, inferring auspicious portents and uncanny signs—and at times they have proved effective in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition also spawned wind-angle, Dunjia, the seven governors, original breath, six-day-seven-part reckoning, encounter divination, day-selectors, the ting-zhuan and shunyu methods, orphan-and-void calculation—ways of reading the sky and qi to trace good or ill omens—and sometimes they really seemed to work.

sentences.zh: 而斯道隱遠，玄奧難原，故聖人不語怪神，罕言性命。

translations.literal: Yet this path is hidden and remote, profound and hard to trace to its source; therefore the sage did not speak of prodigies and spirits, and rarely discussed nature and destiny.
translations.idiomatic: But the way runs dark and far off, too abstruse to pin down, which is why the sage kept silent about ghosts and marvels and seldom spoke of fate or human nature.

sentences.zh: 或開末而抑其端，或曲辭以章其義，所謂「民可使由之，不可使知之」。

translations.literal: Some opened the branch ends while restraining the root, others used tortuous wording to display the meaning—what is called 'The people may be made to follow it, but may not be made to understand it.'
translations.idiomatic: Some teachers stressed the fringe while holding the core in check; others twisted their words to make a point—much like the saying that the common people may be led along the path but not lectured into grasping it.

sentences.zh: 漢自武帝頗好方術，天下懷協道藝之士，莫不負策抵掌，順風而屆焉。

translations.literal: From the Han, since Emperor Wu was quite fond of occult arts, every scholar in the realm who hugged secret skills to his breast came with satchel under arm and palms clapped in eagerness, riding the wind to present himself.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, once Emperor Wu took a strong interest in esoteric techniques, every adept who hoarded a trick or two shouldered his satchel and hurried to court, eager to catch the imperial breeze.

sentences.zh: 後王莽矯用符命，及光武尤信讖言，士之赴趣時宜者，皆騁馳穿鑿，爭談之也。

translations.literal: Later Wang Mang falsely employed token prophecies, and Guangwu in turn trusted apocryphal pronouncements exceedingly; gentlemen who rushed to suit the temper of the age all galloped off, drilling holes and forcing meanings, vying to discourse on them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang then twisted the chenwei oracles to his ends, and Emperor Guangwu believed the apocrypha with unusual fervor, so opportunists raced to wrench texts into shape and outdid one another in expounding them.

sentences.zh: 故王梁、孫咸，名應圖籙，越登槐鼎之任；

translations.literal: Therefore Wang Liang and Sun Xian, their names answering to charts and registers, leapt straight into the rank of the Three Dukes;
translations.idiomatic: So Wang Liang and Sun Xian, whose names matched prophetic slips, vaulted into the highest ministerial seats overnight;

sentences.zh: 鄭興、賈逵，以附同稱顯；

translations.literal: Zheng Xing and Jia Kui, by going along with the trend, won renown;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xing and Jia Kui climbed to prominence by swimming with the tide;

sentences.zh: 恆譚、尹敏，以乖忤淪敗。

translations.literal: Huan Tan and Yin Min, by opposing it, sank into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tan and Yin Min were ruined because they stood athwart it.

sentences.zh: 自是習為內學，尚奇文，貴異數，不乏於時矣。

translations.literal: From this it became habitual to treat these as 'inner learning,' to prize strange texts and esteem uncanny reckonings, and they were never wanting in that age.
translations.idiomatic: After that the fashion was to call them 'inner classics,' to dote on bizarre writings and rare numerologies, and the age never lacked for either.

sentences.zh: 是以通儒碩生，忿其奸妄不經，奏議慷慨，以為宜見藏擯。

translations.literal: Therefore thorough Confucians and eminent scholars, resenting their deceitful falsehood and lack of classical warrant, submitted memorials in high indignation, holding that such things ought to be shelved and rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Learned men, furious at the fraud and want of canonical grounding, petitioned in blunt anger that the lot be locked away and cast aside.

sentences.zh: 子長亦云：「觀陰陽之書，使人拘而多忌。

translations.literal: Zi Chang also said, 'Reading the books of yin and yang makes one cramped and full of taboos.'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian observed that poring over yin-yang manuals leaves a reader cramped and full of taboos.

sentences.zh: 」蓋為此也。

translations.literal: —it was broadly for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: He had this very abuse in mind.

sentences.zh: 夫物之所偏，未能無蔽。

translations.literal: Whenever things lean to one side, they cannot fail to be obscured.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever doctrine tilts too far inevitably blinds itself somewhere.

sentences.zh: 雖云大道，其硋或同。

translations.literal: Although one may speak of the great Way, its hindrances may be the same.
translations.idiomatic: Even the highest teaching can trip over the same obstacles.

sentences.zh: 若乃《詩》之失愚，《書》之失誣。

translations.literal: Thus the failure of the Odes is foolishness; the failure of the Documents is untruthfulness.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes, they say, err toward naïveté; the Documents err toward exaggeration.

sentences.zh: 然則數術之失，至於詭俗乎？

translations.literal: In that case does the failure of numerological arts reach the point of deceiving vulgar custom?
translations.idiomatic: If so, do the number arts stray until they simply cozen the crowd?

sentences.zh: 如令溫柔敦厚而不愚，斯深於《詩》者也；

translations.literal: If one is gentle and honest yet not foolish, such a one is deep in the Odes;
translations.idiomatic: To be tender, honest, and still not naive is to have mastered the Odes;

sentences.zh: 疏通知遠而不誣，斯深於《書》者也；

translations.literal: broadly informed and far-seeing yet not untruthful, such a one is deep in the Documents;
translations.idiomatic: to be lucid, far-reaching, and still not mendacious is to have mastered the Documents;

sentences.zh: 極數知變而不詭俗，斯深於數術者也。

translations.literal: to exhaust numbers and know change yet not deceive vulgar custom, such a one is deep in the arts of reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: and to push calculation to its limits, grasp change, and never pander to superstition is to have mastered the technical arts.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「苟非其人，道不虛行。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, 'If it is not the right person, the Way does not travel empty.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the adage: without the right man, the Way does not move of itself.

sentences.zh: 」意者多迷其統，取遣頗偏，甚有雖流宕過誕亦失也。

translations.literal: Many who indulge such intentions lose the main thread of the system; their choices are quite one-sided, and there are even cases where, though dissolute and excessive in their drift, they still miss the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Most enthusiasts lose the whole in the parts, pick their evidence with bias, and some grow so wild in speculation that they miss the truth altogether.

sentences.zh: 中世張衡為陰陽之宗，郎顗咎徵最密，餘亦班班名家焉。

translations.literal: In middle antiquity Zhang Heng was patriarch of yin and yang, while Lang Yi was most precise in portents of blame and blessing; the rest too shine in their several schools.
translations.idiomatic: At mid-Han Zhang Heng led the yin-yang field, Lang Yi was tightest on omen interpretation, and others glittered each in a niche.

sentences.zh: 其徒亦有雅才偉德，未必體極藝能。

translations.literal: Among their followers were also men of refined talent and lofty virtue who did not necessarily embody the utmost in craft.
translations.idiomatic: Their disciples included men of real culture and character who never reached the summit of technique.

sentences.zh: 今蓋糾其推變尤長，可以弘補時事，因合表之云。

translations.literal: Now I shall pick out those whose calculations of change were especially strong and who could broadly aid affairs of the time, and therefore set them forth in one table.
translations.idiomatic: Here I single out those whose predictive skill did most for the age and list them together.

sentences.zh: 任文公

translations.literal: Ren Wengong
translations.idiomatic: Ren Wengong

sentences.zh: 任文公，巴郡閬中人也。

translations.literal: Ren Wengong was a native of Langzhong in Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Wengong came from Langzhong in Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 父文孫，明曉天官風角秘要。

translations.literal: His father Wensun was clear-sighted in the secrets of celestial offices and wind-angle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren Wensun knew the astrological canons and the wind-angle art inside out.

sentences.zh: 文公少修父術，州辟從事。

translations.literal: Wengong in his youth cultivated his father's arts and was summoned as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The son trained in his father's science and the province appointed him a retainer.

sentences.zh: 哀帝時，有言越巂太守欲反，刺史大懼，遣文公等五從事檢行郡界，潛伺虛實。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ai, word came that the governor of Yuexi wished to rebel; the inspector was greatly alarmed and sent Wengong and five other retainers to patrol the commandery borders and spy out the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ai a rumor spread that the Yuexi governor meant to rise; the terrified inspector dispatched Wengong and five colleagues to scout the frontier.

sentences.zh: 共止傳舍，時，暴風卒至，文公遽趣白諸從事促去，當有逆變來害人者，因起駕速驅。

translations.literal: They lodged together at a post station when suddenly a violent wind struck; Wengong hurriedly urged the other retainers to leave at once, saying a mutinous turn was coming that would harm men, and thereupon mounted his carriage and whipped off.
translations.idiomatic: They were sharing a relay inn when a gale struck; Wengong shouted that a deadly revolt was brewing and they must flee at once, then leaped into his cart and bolted.

sentences.zh: 諸從事未能自發，郡果使兵殺之，文公獨得免。

translations.literal: The other retainers could not bring themselves to move in time; the commandery indeed sent troops to kill them, and Wengong alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His companions hesitated until troops from the commandery cut them down; only Wengong got away.

sentences.zh: 後為治中從事。

translations.literal: Later he served as retainer in the bureau of administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to retainer in the headquarters bureau.

sentences.zh: 時，天大旱，白刺史曰：「五月一日，當有大水。

translations.literal: At that time heaven brought a great drought, and he reported to the inspector, 'On the first day of the fifth month there will be a great flood.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought he warned the inspector, 'On the first of the fifth month a flood will break.

sentences.zh: 其變已至，不可防救，宜令吏人豫為其備。

translations.literal: The transformation has already arrived; it cannot be prevented or saved against—you should order officials and commoners to prepare beforehand.'
translations.idiomatic: The signs are already here; nothing can hold it back—have every clerk and household prepare now.'

sentences.zh: 」刺史不聽，文公獨儲大船。

translations.literal: ' The inspector would not listen; Wengong alone stored up large boats.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector scoffed, but Wengong quietly laid in big boats.

sentences.zh: 百姓或聞，頗有為防者。

translations.literal: When the commoners heard, quite a few made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread, and many people took precautions.

sentences.zh: 到其日旱烈，文公急命促載，使白刺史，刺史笑之。

translations.literal: When that day came the drought was fierce; Wengong urgently ordered loading and sent word to the inspector, who laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: The sun beat down as he predicted; he pressed people to load up and again warned the inspector, who only laughed.

sentences.zh: 日將中，天北雲起，須臾大雨，至晡時，湔水湧起十餘丈，突壞廬舍，所害數千人。

translations.literal: As the sun neared mid-heaven, clouds rose in the north; in a moment there was heavy rain, and by late afternoon the Jian waters surged more than ten yards high, smashing huts and houses and killing several thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Near noon clouds piled up from the north, rain burst forth, and by mid-afternoon the Jian River had risen thirty feet, sweeping away homes and drowning thousands.

sentences.zh: 文公遂以佔術馳名。

translations.literal: Wengong thereupon became famous for his divination arts.
translations.idiomatic: From that day his mantic skill was famous.

sentences.zh: 辟司空掾。

translations.literal: He was summoned as clerk to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works gave him a clerkship.

sentences.zh: 平帝即位，稱疾歸家。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ping took the throne, he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ping ascended the throne he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 王莽篡後，文公推數，知當大亂，乃課家人負物百斤，環舍趨走，日數十，時人莫知其故。

translations.literal: After Wang Mang usurped the throne, Wengong reckoned by numerology that great chaos was coming; he therefore drilled his household to shoulder loads of a hundred catties and run circles around the house scores of times a day, and people of the time did not know his reason.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Mang seized power he foresaw turmoil and made his family shoulder hundred-jin packs and trot laps around the compound daily while neighbors wondered what game he was playing.

sentences.zh: 後兵寇並起，其逃亡者少能自脫，惟文公大小負糧捷步，悉得完免。

translations.literal: Later, when soldiers and bandits rose together, those who fled seldom got free, but Wengong's whole family, large and small, bore grain and ran with nimble steps and all came through unscathed.
translations.idiomatic: When war and pillage followed, refugees rarely survived, yet his whole clan, laden with grain, outran danger and escaped intact.

sentences.zh: 遂奔子公山，十餘年不被兵革。

translations.literal: They then fled to Zigong Mountain and for more than ten years were untouched by arms.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew to Mount Zigong and lived a dozen years without seeing a blade.

sentences.zh: 公孫述時，蜀武擔石折。

translations.literal: In the time of Gongsun Shu, the Shu 'martial' stone at Wudan broke.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gongsun Shu the martial stone at Wudan in Shu snapped.

sentences.zh: 文公曰：「噫！

translations.literal: Wengong said, 'Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Wengong murmured, 'Ah—

sentences.zh: 西州智士死，我乃當之。

translations.literal: The wise men of the western provinces will die, and I shall be the one to answer for it.'
translations.idiomatic: when the western realm's best minds perish, the reckoning falls on me.'

sentences.zh: 」自是常會聚子孫，設酒食。

translations.literal: ' From this he regularly gathered sons and grandsons and set out wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: After that he kept calling his descendants together for feasts.

sentences.zh: 後三月果卒。

translations.literal: Three months later he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: Three months later he was dead.

sentences.zh: 故益部為之語曰：「任文公，智無雙。」

translations.literal: Therefore the saying in Yi province went, 'Ren Wengong—wit without peer.'
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou folk coined the line, 'Ren Wengong—no mind matches his.'

sentences.zh: 郭憲字子橫，汝南宋人也。

translations.literal: Guo Xian, courtesy name Ziheng, was a native of Song in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian, styled Ziheng, hailed from Song in Runan.

sentences.zh: 少師事東海王仲子。

translations.literal: In his youth he studied under Wang Zhongzi of the East Sea as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he took the eastern sea scholar Wang Zhongzi as his master.

sentences.zh: 時，王莽為大司馬，召仲子。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Mang was Grand Marshal and summoned Zhongzi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang, then Grand Marshal, summoned Zhongzi.

sentences.zh: 仲子欲往。

translations.literal: Zhongzi wished to go.
translations.idiomatic: The master meant to obey.

sentences.zh: 憲諫曰：「禮有來學，無有往教之義。

translations.literal: Xian remonstrated, saying, 'According to ritual there is coming to learn; there is no principle of the teacher going to instruct.'
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian objected: 'Propriety allows pupils to come to the teacher, not great men to drag the teacher to them.'

sentences.zh: 今君賤道畏貴，竊所不取。

translations.literal: 'Now you would slight the Way and fear the mighty—I cannot privately approve.'
translations.idiomatic: To demean the Way and cower before rank is something I cannot stomach.'

sentences.zh: 」仲子曰：「王公至重，不敢違之。

translations.literal: ' Zhongzi said, 'The royal duke is supremely weighty; I dare not disobey him.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzi replied, 'The minister's summons is not to be refused.'

sentences.zh: 」憲曰：「今正臨講業，且當訖事。

translations.literal: ' Xian said, 'Now we are just in the middle of lecturing; let us first finish the business.'
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian said, 'We are mid-lecture; let us finish the lesson first.'

sentences.zh: 」仲子從之，日晏乃往。

translations.literal: ' Zhongzi followed him, and only when the day was late did he go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzi agreed and arrived only at dusk.

sentences.zh: 莽問：「君來何遲？

translations.literal: Mang asked, 'Why have you come so late?'
translations.idiomatic: Mang asked why he was late.

sentences.zh: 」仲子具以憲言對，莽陰奇之。

translations.literal: ' Zhongzi reported in full what Xian had said, and Mang secretly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzi repeated Guo Xian's words, and Mang quietly marked the young man.

sentences.zh: 及後篡位，拜憲郎中，賜以衣服。

translations.literal: When later he usurped the throne, he appointed Xian Gentleman of the Palace and bestowed clothing on him.
translations.idiomatic: After usurping the throne Mang named him a palace gentleman and sent robes as gifts.

sentences.zh: 憲受衣焚之，逃於東海之濱。

translations.literal: Xian accepted the clothes but burned them and fled to the edge of the East Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian took the silks, burned them, and fled to the eastern seaboard.

sentences.zh: 莽深忿恚，討逐不知所在。

translations.literal: Mang was deeply resentful and sought him everywhere without learning where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Mang raged and hunted him without success.

sentences.zh: 八年，車駕西征隗囂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the imperial carriage marched west against Wei Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jianwu the emperor marched west against Wei Xiao.

sentences.zh: 憲諫曰：「天下初定，車駕未可以動。

translations.literal: Xian remonstrated, saying, 'The realm has only just been settled; the imperial carriage ought not to move.'
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian urged him not to go: the empire was still unsettled and the ruler should not take the field.

sentences.zh: 」憲乃當車拔佩刀以斷車靷。

translations.literal: ' Xian then stood blocking the chariot, drew his girdle knife, and severed the traces.
translations.idiomatic: He planted himself before the team, drew his belt knife, and cut the traces.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，遂上隴。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow him and ascended Long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored him and climbed Long Mountain.

sentences.zh: 其後潁川兵起，乃回駕而還。

translations.literal: Later, when troops rose in Yingchuan, he turned the carriage and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingchuan rose in revolt he had to wheel about and ride back.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「恨不用子橫之言。」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed, saying, 'I regret I did not use Ziheng's words.'
translations.idiomatic: He sighed that he should have listened to Ziheng.

sentences.zh: 時，匈奴數犯塞，帝患之，乃召百僚廷議。

translations.literal: At that time the Xiongnu repeatedly raided the frontier, and the emperor worried over it and summoned the hundred officials to deliberate in court.
translations.idiomatic: As the Xiongnu kept raiding the passes, he called a full court to debate a response.

sentences.zh: 憲以為天下疲敝，不宜動眾。

translations.literal: Xian held that the realm was exhausted and that it was not fitting to move the hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian argued the country was too spent for another campaign.

sentences.zh: 諫爭不合，乃伏地稱眩瞀，不復言。

translations.literal: His remonstrance did not prevail, so he lay prostrate claiming dizziness and blurred vision and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: When he lost the argument he dropped flat, feigned vertigo, and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 帝令兩郎扶下殿，憲亦不拜。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered two gentlemen to help him down from the hall, yet Xian did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Two attendants were told to haul him off the dais, yet he refused even a curt bow.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「常聞『關東觥觥郭子橫』，竟不虛也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, 'I have often heard “East of the Pass Guo Ziheng stands fearless”—it was indeed no empty praise.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked, 'They say east of the pass Guo Ziheng fears nothing—true enough.'

sentences.zh: 」憲遂以病辭退，卒於家。

translations.literal: ' Xian thereupon resigned on grounds of illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian then retired citing illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 許楊字偉君，汝南平輿人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yang, courtesy name Weijun, was a native of Pingyu in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yang, styled Weijun, came from Pingyu in Runan.

sentences.zh: 少好術數。

translations.literal: In his youth he loved the arts of numbers.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved numerology and technique.

sentences.zh: 王莽輔政，召為郎，稍遷酒泉都尉。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang was regent, he was summoned as Gentleman of the Palace and gradually rose to Commandant of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang, as regent, called him to court as a gentleman and later promoted him to Jiuquan commandant.

sentences.zh: 及莽篡位，楊乃變姓名為巫醫，逃匿它界。

translations.literal: When Mang usurped the throne, Yang changed his name and became a shaman-physician, fleeing and hiding in another region.
translations.idiomatic: When Mang seized the throne Xu Yang changed his name, posed as a witch-doctor, and hid in another province.

sentences.zh: 莽敗，方還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Mang fell, he then returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: After Mang fell he came home.

sentences.zh: 汝南舊有鴻郤陂，成帝時，丞相翟方進奏毀敗之。

translations.literal: Runan formerly had the Hongxi Lake; in the time of Emperor Cheng, Chancellor Zhai Fangjin memorialized to destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: Runan once held the great Hongxi marsh until Chancellor Zhai Fangjin persuaded Emperor Cheng to drain it.

sentences.zh: 建武中，太守鄧晨欲修復其功。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period, Governor Deng Chen wished to restore its achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu Governor Deng Chen wanted to rebuild the works.

sentences.zh: 聞楊曉水脈，召與議之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yang understood watercourses, he summoned him to consult.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Xu Yang read water patterns, Deng Chen called him in to plan.

sentences.zh: 楊曰：「昔成帝用方進之言，尋而自夢上天，天帝怒曰：『何故敗我濯龍淵？

translations.literal: Yang said, 'Formerly Emperor Cheng followed Fangjin's advice, and soon afterward dreamed he ascended to Heaven; the Lord on High was angry and said, “Why did you destroy my Dragon-Pool bathing place?”'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yang said, 'Emperor Cheng listened to Zhai Fangjin and soon dreamed he had ascended to heaven, where the High God demanded, “Why ruin my Dragon Pool?”'

sentences.zh: 』是後民失其利，多致飢困。

translations.literal: ' After that the people lost its benefit and many fell into hunger and distress.
translations.idiomatic: The people lost the lake and starved in droves.

sentences.zh: 時有謠歌曰：『敗我陂者翟子威，飴我大豆，亨我芋魁。

translations.literal: At the time there was a ditty: 'He who ruined our lake was Zhai Ziwei; he fed us great beans and boiled us taro roots.'
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme ran: Zhai Ziwei wrecked our dyke, fed us beans, stewed our taro.

sentences.zh: 反乎覆，陂當復。

translations.literal: ' Turn it over and back—the lake ought to return.'
translations.idiomatic: Turn and turn again—the marsh must return.'

sentences.zh: 』昔大禹決江疏河，以利天下。

translations.literal: ' Formerly Yu the Great opened the Yangtze and dredged the Yellow River to benefit all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Great Yu cut channels for the rivers to benefit the world.

sentences.zh: 明府今興立廢業，富國安民，童謠之言，將有徵於此。

translations.literal: If my enlightened lord now raises a ruined enterprise to enrich the state and secure the people, the words of the children's song will here find their verification.'
translations.idiomatic: If you revive this drowned work to enrich the commandery and feed the people, the old children's song will prove true at last.'

sentences.zh: 誠願以死效力。

translations.literal: ' I sincerely wish to exert my strength unto death.'
translations.idiomatic: I am willing to stake my life on the task.'

sentences.zh: 」晨大悅，因署楊為都水掾，使典其事。

translations.literal: ' Chen was greatly pleased and therefore appointed Yang Clerk of Waters to superintend the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chen delightedly named him clerk of waterworks and put him in charge.

sentences.zh: 楊因高下形勢，起塘四百餘里，數年乃立。

translations.literal: Yang, following the lay of high and low ground, raised dikes for more than four hundred li, and only after several years was it completed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yang traced the terrain and threw up four hundred li of embankment; the job took years.

sentences.zh: 百姓得其便，累歲大稔。

translations.literal: The commoners gained the convenience, and year after year the harvests were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The farmers prospered and harvests turned fat year on year.

sentences.zh: 初，豪右大姓因緣陂役，競欲辜較在所，楊一無聽，遂共譖楊受取賕賂。

translations.literal: At first the powerful magnates, using the lake labor as a pretext, vied to squeeze the local offices; Yang listened to none of them, so they together slandered Yang for accepting bribes.
translations.idiomatic: At first the great clans tried to rig the corvée; Xu Yang blocked every squeeze play, so they joined in accusing him of taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 晨遂收楊下獄，而械輒自解。

translations.literal: Chen thereupon seized Yang and put him in prison, yet the fetters repeatedly came undone of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chen jailed Xu Yang, but the manacles kept falling open on their own.

sentences.zh: 獄吏恐，遽白晨。

translations.literal: The jailers were afraid and hurriedly reported to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The terrified wardens ran to Deng Chen.

sentences.zh: 晨驚曰：「果濫矣。

translations.literal: Chen said in alarm, 'It has indeed been a false charge.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chen exclaimed, 'The charge was unjust.

sentences.zh: 太守聞忠信可以感靈，今其效乎！

translations.literal: I have heard that loyalty and good faith can move the spirits—does this now prove it!'
translations.idiomatic: They say loyalty can touch the gods—here is the proof!'

sentences.zh: 」即夜出楊，遣歸。

translations.literal: ' That very night he released Yang and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: That night he freed Xu Yang and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 時天大陰晦，道中若有火光照之，時人異焉。

translations.literal: At the time the sky was greatly overcast and dark; on the road it was as if a fire's light shone upon him, and people of the time marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: The heavens were black as ink, yet a glow lit his path like a torch, and onlookers took it for a wonder.

sentences.zh: 後以病卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of an illness.

sentences.zh: 晨於都宮為楊起廟，圖畫形像，百姓思其功績，皆祭祀之。

translations.literal: Chen had a temple raised to Yang in the capital shrine, with painted images; the common people, remembering his achievements, all sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chen built him a shrine in the metropolitan temple and hung his portrait; grateful folk kept his altars busy.

sentences.zh: 高獲字敬公，汝南新息人也。

translations.literal: Gao Huo, courtesy name Jinggong, was a native of Xinxi in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huo, styled Jinggong, came from Xinxi in Runan.

sentences.zh: 為人尼首方面。

translations.literal: In person he had a receding crown and a square face.
translations.idiomatic: He was built like a man with a sloping forehead and a square jaw.

sentences.zh: 少游學京師，與光武有舊。

translations.literal: In his youth he traveled to study in the capital and had old ties with Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: As a young scholar in the capital he had known Emperor Guangwu long before.

sentences.zh: 師事司徒歐陽歙。

translations.literal: He took Minister over the Masses Ouyang Xi as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Ouyang Xi, the minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 歙下獄當斷，獲冠鐵冠，帶鈇鑕，詣闕請歙。

translations.literal: When Xi was cast into prison and faced execution, Huo donned an iron cap, girded on axe and fetter, and went to the palace gate to beg for Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang Xi was jailed and sentenced to die, Gao Huo put on an iron cap, buckled on the felon's axe and fetters, and pleaded at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不赦，而引見之。

translations.literal: Although the emperor did not grant a pardon, he nonetheless summoned and received him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused the pardon but still granted him an audience.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「敬公，朕欲用子為吏，宜改常性。

translations.literal: He said to him, 'Jinggong, I wish to employ you as an official—you ought to change your usual disposition.'
translations.idiomatic: He told him, 'Jinggong, I mean to give you office; you must mend your stubborn ways.'

sentences.zh: 」獲對曰：「臣受性於父母，不可改之於陛下。

translations.literal: ' Huo replied, 'Your servant received his nature from his parents; it cannot be altered before Your Majesty.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huo answered, 'What my parents gave me in temperament no edict can reshape.'

sentences.zh: 」出便辭去。

translations.literal: ' He went out and at once took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed out and left without looking back.

sentences.zh: 三公爭辟，不應。

translations.literal: The Three Dukes vied to summon him, but he would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: All three dukes tried to recruit him; he ignored every offer.

sentences.zh: 後太守鮑昱請獲，既至門，令主簿就迎，主簿但使騎吏迎之，獲聞之，即去。

translations.literal: Later, when Governor Bao Yu invited Huo, and Huo had reached the gate, Yu ordered his chief clerk to go welcome him in person, but the chief clerk merely sent mounted clerks to receive him; when Huo heard of it, he departed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Bao Yu later invited him in, yet at the door the chief clerk sent only outriders instead of greeting him in person; Gao Huo turned on his heel.

sentences.zh: 昱遣追請獲，獲顧曰：「府君但為主簿所欺，不足與談。

translations.literal: Yu sent men in pursuit to invite Huo again; Huo looked back and said, 'The lord of the house is merely deceived by his chief clerk—not worth talking with.'
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yu sent runners to fetch him back; Gao Huo called over his shoulder, 'Your honor is hoodwinked by a clerk—not worth my time.'

sentences.zh: 」遂不留。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he did not stay.
translations.idiomatic: He never set foot inside.

sentences.zh: 時郡境大旱。

translations.literal: At the time the commandery territory suffered great drought.
translations.idiomatic: A killing drought gripped the commandery.

sentences.zh: 獲素善天文，曉遁甲，能役使鬼神。

translations.literal: Huo had always been skilled in astronomy, understood Dunjia, and could command ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huo read the stars, knew Dunjia, and was said to command spirits.

sentences.zh: 昱自往問何以致雨，獲曰：「急罷三部督郵，明府當自北出，到三十里亭，雨可致也。

translations.literal: Yu himself went to ask by what means rain could be brought; Huo said, 'Hurry to dismiss the three circuit supervising clerks; my enlightened lord should himself ride north to the post station at thirty li, and rain can be brought.'
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yu rode out to ask the rite for rain. Gao Huo said, 'Dismiss your three touring supervisors at once, then ride north yourself to the thirty-li post station—that will draw the storm.'

sentences.zh: 」昱從之，果得大雨。

translations.literal: ' Yu followed him, and indeed obtained great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yu obeyed, and the heavens opened.

sentences.zh: 每行縣，輒軾其閭。

translations.literal: Whenever he toured the counties, he always touched the crossbar of his carriage in respect at Huo's lane.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Bao Yu inspected the counties he lifted the carriage bar in salute as he passed Gao Huo's lane.

sentences.zh: 獲遂遠遁江南，卒於石城。

translations.literal: Huo thereupon fled far to the south of the Yangzi and died at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huo withdrew deep into the southland and died at Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 石城人思之，共為立祠。

translations.literal: The people of Shicheng missed him and together built a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shicheng missed him and raised a temple in his honor.

sentences.zh: 王喬者，河東人也。

translations.literal: Wang Qiao was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 顯宗世，為葉令。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Ming he was magistrate of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he served as magistrate of Ye.

sentences.zh: 喬有神術，每月朔望，常自縣詣臺朝。

translations.literal: Qiao had divine arts; on the first and fifteenth of each month he would regularly come from the county to the terrace court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed uncanny skills: every new and full moon he traveled from Ye to the capital for court without fail.

sentences.zh: 帝怪其來數，而不見車騎，密令太史伺望之。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled that he came so often yet no carriage or escort was seen, and secretly ordered the grand astrologer to watch for him.
translations.idiomatic: The court wondered how he arrived so often yet never with a train, so the emperor told the grand astrologer to spy on him.

sentences.zh: 言其臨至，輒有雙鳧從東南飛來。

translations.literal: They reported that whenever he was about to arrive, a pair of wild ducks always flew in from the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: They reported that each time he neared the capital two wild ducks flew in from the southeast.

sentences.zh: 於是候鳧至，舉羅張之，但得一隻舄焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon, when the ducks came, they raised a net and caught them, but obtained only a single shoe.
translations.idiomatic: When the birds appeared the watchers cast a net and snared only one slipper.

sentences.zh: 乃詔上方𧭉視，則四年中所賜尚書官屬履也。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered the imperial workshops to examine it, and it proved to be a shoe bestowed four years earlier on the staff of the minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: The palace workshops identified it as footwear given four years before to attendants of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 每當朝時，葉門下鼓不擊自鳴，聞於京師。

translations.literal: Whenever it was time for court audience, the drum beneath the Ye gate would sound of itself without being struck, and the noise was heard in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On court days the gate drum at Ye would roll without a hand touching it, and the capital could hear it.

sentences.zh: 後天下玉棺於堂前，吏人推排，終不搖動。

translations.literal: Later a jade coffin descended before the hall; clerks and officials pushed and shoved it, yet in the end it would not budge.
translations.idiomatic: Then a jade sarcophagus appeared before the yamen; clerks heaved together but could not shift it.

sentences.zh: 喬曰：「天帝獨召我邪？

translations.literal: Qiao said, 'Does the Lord on High summon me alone?'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao asked, 'Does Heaven call for me alone?'

sentences.zh: 」乃沐浴服飾寢其中，蓋便立覆。

translations.literal: ' He thereupon bathed, dressed, and lay down inside it, and the lid at once closed upright over him.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed, robed himself, lay inside, and the lid dropped straight shut.

sentences.zh: 宿昔葬於城東，土自成墳。

translations.literal: Overnight he was buried east of the city, and earth of itself formed a mound.
translations.idiomatic: By morning he lay buried east of the walls, a mound rising as if shaped by unseen hands.

sentences.zh: 其夕，縣中牛皆流汗喘乏，而人無知者。

translations.literal: That night every ox in the county sweated and panted with exhaustion, yet no human knew why.
translations.idiomatic: That same night every ox in the county streamed sweat and heaved for breath, though no one understood why.

sentences.zh: 百姓乃為立廟，號葉君祠。

translations.literal: The common people thereupon built a temple for him, styling it the shrine of Lord Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The people raised a temple and hailed him as Lord Ye.

sentences.zh: 牧守每班錄，皆先謁拜之。

translations.literal: Whenever governors and shepherds took up their registers of appointment, they always first paid cult to him.
translations.idiomatic: Each new governor, roster in hand, bowed at his shrine before doing anything else.

sentences.zh: 吏人祈禱，無不如應。

translations.literal: When clerks and people prayed to him, there was nothing that did not receive a response.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions from clerks and commoners were answered every time.

sentences.zh: 若有違犯，亦立能為祟。

translations.literal: If anyone violated the taboos, he could also at once work harm as a haunting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Break his rules and he would lash back as a vengeful ghost.

sentences.zh: 帝乃迎取其鼓，置都亭下，略無復聲焉。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon had the drum brought in and set beneath the metropolitan post station, and thereafter it scarcely sounded again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seized the drum and hung it under the capital post station, after which it barely spoke again.

sentences.zh: 或云此即古仙人王子喬也。

translations.literal: Some say this was none other than the ancient immortal Wang Ziqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Some identify him with the immortal Wang Ziqiao of old.

sentences.zh: 謝夷吾

translations.literal: Xie Yiwu
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yiwu

sentences.zh: 謝夷吾字堯卿，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Xie Yiwu, courtesy name Yaoqing, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yiwu, styled Yaoqing, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 少為郡吏，學風角佔候。

translations.literal: In his youth he was a commandery clerk and studied wind-angle divination and omen reading.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a commandery clerk and trained in wind-angle and portent lore.

sentences.zh: 太守第五倫擢為督郵。

translations.literal: Governor Diwu Lun promoted him to supervising clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Diwu Lun raised him to supervising clerk.

sentences.zh: 時，烏程長有臧釁，倫使收案其罪。

translations.literal: At the time the magistrate of Wucheng bore a taint of corruption; Lun sent Yiwu to seize him and investigate his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Wucheng was rumored corrupt; Diwu Lun ordered Xie Yiwu to arrest and examine him.

sentences.zh: 夷吾到縣，無所驗，但望閣伏哭而還。

translations.literal: When Yiwu reached the county he verified nothing, but only looked toward the gate tower, prostrated himself weeping, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yiwu reached the county, proved nothing in court, faced the gate tower, wept prostrate, and rode back.

sentences.zh: 一縣驚怪，不知所為。

translations.literal: The whole county was startled and wondered what he was doing.
translations.idiomatic: The whole county was baffled.

sentences.zh: 及還，白倫曰：「竊以佔候，知長當死。

translations.literal: When he returned he reported to Lun, saying, 'Your servant has privately divined by omens and knows the magistrate is about to die.
translations.idiomatic: Back at headquarters he told Diwu Lun, 'My divination shows the magistrate is dying.

sentences.zh: 近三十日，遠不過六十日，遊魂假息，非刑所加，故不收之。

translations.literal: Near at hand within thirty days, far at hand not beyond sixty days; his wandering soul borrows breath—it is not a case for the application of punishment—therefore I did not seize him.'
translations.idiomatic: Within thirty days at soonest, sixty at latest; his soul already wanders—no law can touch him—so I made no arrest.'

sentences.zh: 」倫聽其言，至月餘，果有驛馬齎長印綬，上言暴卒。

translations.literal: ' Lun listened to his words, and after a little more than a month, indeed relay horses brought the magistrate's seal and ribbon with a report that he had died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Diwu Lun waited; a month later couriers arrived with the dead man's seal and word of a sudden death.

sentences.zh: 倫以此益禮信之。

translations.literal: Lun for this reason treated him with still greater courtesy and trust.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Diwu Lun honored him the more.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，為壽張令，稍遷荊州刺史，遷鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: He was recommended as filial and incorrupt, became magistrate of Shouzhang, gradually rose to inspector of Jing province, and was transferred governor of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Filial-incorrupt recommendation won him Shouzhang magistracy, then promotion to Jing inspector and Julu governor.

sentences.zh: 所在愛育人物，有善績。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he cherished and nurtured people and had good administrative records.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he nurtured the people and left a fine record.

sentences.zh: 及倫作司徒，令班固為文薦夷吾曰：

translations.literal: When Lun became minister of education, he ordered Ban Gu to compose a text recommending Yiwu, saying,
translations.idiomatic: When Diwu Lun became minister of education he told Ban Gu to draft a memorial praising Xie Yiwu:

sentences.zh: 臣聞堯登稷、契，政隆太平；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when Yao elevated Ji and Xie, government flourished into great peace;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that when Yao raised Ji and Xie, peace spread across the realm;

sentences.zh: 舜用皋陶，政致雍熙、殷、周雖有高宗、昌、發之君，猶賴傅說、呂望之策，故能克崇其業，允協大中。

translations.literal: Shun employed Gao Yao and government reached perfect harmony; although Yin and Zhou had sovereigns such as Gaozong, Chang, and Fa, they still relied on the plans of Fu Yue and Lü Wang, and therefore were able to exalt their enterprises and truly accord with the great mean.
translations.idiomatic: Shun used Gao Yao and harmony followed. Yin and Zhou boasted kings like Gaozong, Wen, and Wu, yet even they leaned on Fu Yue and Lü Wang—only thus could they magnify their work and hit the great mean.

sentences.zh: 竊見鉅鹿太守會稽謝夷吾，出自東州，厥土塗泥，而英姿挺特，奇偉秀出。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed Julu Governor Xie Yiwu of Kuaiji: though he comes from the eastern regions where the soil is mud and mire, his heroic bearing stands apart, strange and grand, outstanding among his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has watched Julu Governor Xie Yiwu of Kuaiji: though he springs from the eastern mudflats, his mien is heroic, his talent towering.

sentences.zh: 才兼四科，行包九德，仁足濟時，知周萬物。

translations.literal: His talents combine the four categories of worthies; his conduct embraces the nine virtues; his benevolence suffices to succor the age; his knowledge encircles the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: He unites the four classes of talent, walks the nine virtues, has benevolence enough to save the times, and knowledge wide as creation.

sentences.zh: 加以少膺儒雅，韜含六籍，推考星度，綜校圖錄，探賾聖秘，觀變曆徵，佔天知地，與神合契，據其道德，以經王務。

translations.literal: Add to this that in youth he received Confucian refinement, harbored the Six Classics within, pushed the reckoning of the stars, collated charts and registers, plumbed the sage's secrets, observed change and examined portents, divined heaven and knew earth, matched spirits in covenant, and grounded royal business in his moral power.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in the classics, he stores the Six Books, tracks the constellations, collates apocrypha, probes the sages' arcana, reads omens in the calendar, knows heaven and earth, moves in tune with the gods, and steers statecraft by virtue.

sentences.zh: 昔為陪隸，與臣從事，奮忠毅之操，躬史魚之節，董臣嚴綱，勗臣懦弱，得以免戾，實賴厥勳。

translations.literal: Formerly, when he was a menial attendant serving with your servant, he displayed the devotion of Zhong and Yu and personally embodied the integrity of Shi Yu, tightened your servant's slack discipline, and stiffened your servant's timidity, so that your servant escaped blame—truly we rely on his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once my underling, he showed the grit of Zhong and Yu and the blunt honor of Shi Yu, tightened my slack rule and steeled my cowardice, and saved me from fault—that merit is mine to repay.

sentences.zh: 及其應選作宰，惠敷百里，降福彌異，流化若神，爰牧荊州，威行邦國。

translations.literal: When afterward he answered selection and became a magistrate, his kindness spread over a hundred li, blessings descended in singular ways, and his transforming influence was like a spirit's; when he shepherded Jing province, his awesomeness ran through the regional states.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate his grace soaked a hundred li, blessings fell strangely, his teaching seemed divine; as Jing inspector his majesty ran the whole province.

sentences.zh: 奉法作政，有周、召之風；

translations.literal: Upholding law and conducting government, he has the air of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao;
translations.idiomatic: His government has the Duke of Zhou's discipline and the Duke of Shao's clarity;

sentences.zh: 居儉履約，紹公儀之操。

translations.literal: dwelling in frugality and keeping faith with restraint, he continues the conduct of Gongyi Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: living spare and keeping faith, he matches Gongyi Xiu.

sentences.zh: 尋功簡能，為外臺之表；

translations.literal: Seeking merit and sorting ability, he is a model for the outer terraces;
translations.idiomatic: In weighing merit and talent he is the outer court's paragon;

sentences.zh: 聽聲察實，為九伯之冠。

translations.literal: listening to reputations and inspecting realities, he is chief among the nine shepherds.
translations.idiomatic: in testing rumor against fact he leads the nine regional inspectors.

sentences.zh: 遷守鉅鹿，政合時雍。

translations.literal: Transferred to guard Julu, his government harmonized with the timely peace.
translations.idiomatic: As Julu governor his rule matched the season of harmony.

sentences.zh: 德量績謀，有伊、呂、管、晏之任；

translations.literal: In virtuous capacity, accumulated plans, he bears the charge of Yi Yin, Lü Wang, Guan Zhong, and Yan Ying;
translations.idiomatic: In moral breadth and policy depth he rivals Yi Yin, Lü Wang, Guan Zhong, and Yan Ying;

sentences.zh: 闡弘道奧，同史蘇、京房之倫。

translations.literal: expounding the profound of the Way, he is of the same class as Shi Su and Jing Fang.
translations.idiomatic: in opening the Way's depths he ranks with Shi Su and Jing Fang.

sentences.zh: 雖密勿在公，而身出心隱，不殉名以求譽，不馳鶩以要寵，念存遜遁，演志箕山。

translations.literal: Although he toils incessantly for the public good, his body is in office while his heart withdraws; he does not sell his name to seek praise, nor gallop after favor; his thoughts incline to yielding retirement, his ambition unfolds toward Mount Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Though he slaves for the state, his mind stays hidden; he trades neither fame nor favor for ambition, and his heart already wanders toward Mount Ji's reclusion.

sentences.zh: 方之古賢，實有倫序；

translations.literal: Compared with the worthies of antiquity, he truly has his proper ordering;
translations.idiomatic: Set beside the ancients he holds his rank;

sentences.zh: 采之於今，超焉絕俗。

translations.literal: gathered from among men of today, he towers alone beyond vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: measured against our own age he stands clean above the crowd.

sentences.zh: 誠社稷之元龜，大漢之棟甍。

translations.literal: He is truly the great tortoise-shell of the altars of soil and grain, the ridge-beam of the great Han.
translations.idiomatic: He is the tortoise-oracle of the state, the roof-tree of Han.

sentences.zh: 宜當拔擢，使登鼎司。

translations.literal: It is fitting that he be promoted and caused to ascend to the ministerial trio.
translations.idiomatic: He should be lifted into the three highest seats.

sentences.zh: 上令三辰順軌於歷象，下使五品咸訓於嘉時，必致休徵克昌之慶，非徒循法奉職而已。

translations.literal: Above he would make the three luminaries run true to the calendar's reckonings; below he would bring the five grades all instructed in a propitious season—surely he would bring about the felicity of auspicious omens and flourishing prosperity, not merely follow the law and hold to office.
translations.idiomatic: Above he would set sun, moon, and stars to their tracks; below he would school the five ranks in a golden age—more than a dutiful clerk, he would summon the omens of a golden peace.

sentences.zh: 臣以頑駑，器非其疇，屍祿負乘，夕惕若厲。

translations.literal: Your servant, dull and worn-out, is not the vessel for such a charge; he occupies salary beyond his worth and rides above his capacity, and trembles nightly as if on the brink.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is a dull nag, unfit for the yoke, fat on unearned pay and riding above his station, and quakes each night like a man on a cliff.

sentences.zh: 願乞骸骨，更授夷吾，上以光七曜之明，下以厭率土之望，庶令微臣塞咎免悔。

translations.literal: I beg to surrender my bones and in turn appoint Yiwu—above to brighten the seven luminaries, below to satisfy the hopes of all within the seas—so that perhaps your humble servant may block fault and escape regret.'
translations.idiomatic: Let me yield my bones and yield the post to Yiwu—above to light the seven governors, below to quiet the empire—so this fool may dodge blame and regret.'

sentences.zh: 後以行春乘柴車，從兩史，冀州刺史上其儀序失中，有損國典，左轉下邳令。

translations.literal: Later, when on the spring inspection tour he rode a brushwood cart with two clerks following, the Ji province inspector reported that the order of his equipage was improper and injured national precedent, and he was demoted to magistrate of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, riding a rough cart with two clerks on his spring rounds, the Ji inspector impeached his retinue as a breach of ritual; he was busted down to magistrate of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 豫克死日，如期果卒。

translations.literal: He beforehand calculated the day of his death, and on the appointed day indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: He foretold his own death and died exactly on schedule.

sentences.zh: 敕其子曰：「漢末當亂，必有發掘露骸之禍。

translations.literal: He instructed his sons, saying, 'When the Han nears its end there will surely be the calamity of tombs dug up and bones left exposed.'
translations.idiomatic: He warned his sons, 'When Han falls, tombs will be opened and bones left in the sun.'

sentences.zh: 」使懸棺下葬，墓不起墳。

translations.literal: ' He ordered them to suspend his coffin for burial and raise no tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: He told them to bury him in a suspended coffin and leave no mound.

sentences.zh: 時，博士勃海郭鳳亦好圖讖，善說災異，吉凶占應。

translations.literal: At the time Academician Guo Feng of Bohai also loved charts and apocrypha and was skilled at explaining calamities and prodigies, auspicious and inauspicious, and divinatory responses.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Bohai academician Guo Feng doted on chenwei charts and read disasters and lucky signs.

sentences.zh: 先自知死期，豫令弟子市棺斂具，至其日而終。

translations.literal: He beforehand knew himself the day of his death, and in advance ordered his disciples to buy a coffin and shroud; on that day he ended.
translations.idiomatic: He too knew his last day, sent disciples to buy a coffin beforehand, and died on the dot.

sentences.zh: 楊由字哀侯，蜀郡成都人也，少習《易》，並七政、元氣、風雲佔候。

translations.literal: Yang You, courtesy name Aihou, was a native of Chengdu in Shu commandery; in his youth he studied the Changes, together with the seven luminaries, primordial qi, and wind-and-cloud divination.
translations.idiomatic: Yang You, styled Aihou, of Chengdu in Shu, studied the Changes, the seven governors, original breath, and weather omens.

sentences.zh: 為郡文學掾。

translations.literal: He was educational aide of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as the commandery's educational aide.

sentences.zh: 時，有大雀夜集於庫樓上，太守廉範以問由。

translations.literal: At the time a great sparrow by night roosted on the armory tower; Governor Lian Fan questioned You about it.
translations.idiomatic: A huge sparrow roosted one night on the arsenal tower; Governor Lian Fan asked Yang You what it meant.

sentences.zh: 由對曰：「此佔郡內當有小兵，然不為害。

translations.literal: You replied, saying, 'This divines that there will be minor soldiers within the commandery, yet they will not do harm.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang You said, 'It marks petty fighting inside the commandery, nothing serious.'

sentences.zh: 」後二十餘日，廣柔縣蠻夷反，殺傷長吏，郡發庫兵擊之。

translations.literal: ' After more than twenty days the Man tribes of Guangrou county rebelled, killing and wounding senior officials, and the commandery issued armory weapons to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days later Guangrou's barbarians rose, cut down officers, and the commandery unlocked the arsenal to fight them off.

sentences.zh: 又有風吹削哺，太守以問由。

translations.literal: Again there was a wind that blew carved feeding-slips; the governor questioned You about it.
translations.idiomatic: Wind next blew carved feeding boards about; the governor again consulted Yang You.

sentences.zh: 由對曰：「方當有薦木實者，其色黃赤。

translations.literal: You replied, saying, 'Presently someone will present fruit of a tree; its color will be yellow and red.'
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'Someone will soon bring fruit—yellow-red in color.'

sentences.zh: 」頃之，五官掾獻橘數包。

translations.literal: ' In a little while the clerk of the five offices presented several bundles of oranges.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a clerk of the five bureaus offered several sacks of oranges.

sentences.zh: 由嘗從人飲，敕御者曰：「酒若三行，便宜嚴駕。

translations.literal: You once drank in another's company and ordered his charioteer, saying, 'If the wine goes three rounds, you should at once ready the team tightly.'
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet Yang You told his driver, 'After the third round, hitch the horses tight.'

sentences.zh: 」既而趣去。

translations.literal: ' Presently he hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: He left in haste before the feast ended.

sentences.zh: 後主人舍有鬥相殺者，人請問何以知之。

translations.literal: Later the host's lodgings had a fight in which men killed each other; people asked how he had known.
translations.idiomatic: A brawl broke out in the host's house and men died; guests asked how he had foreseen it.

sentences.zh: 由曰：「向社中木上有鳩鬥，此兵賊之像也。

translations.literal: You said, 'Just now on the tree above the earth-altar doves were fighting—this is the image of soldiers and bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang You said, 'I saw doves brawling on the tree over the village shrine—a sign of armed strife.'

sentences.zh: 」其言多驗。

translations.literal: His words were mostly verified.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again his readings came true.

sentences.zh: 著書十餘篇，名曰《其平》。

translations.literal: He composed more than ten treatises, entitled *Qi Ping*.
translations.idiomatic: He left a dozen essays collected under the title *Qi Ping*.

sentences.zh: 終於家。

translations.literal: He ended his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 李南字孝山，丹陽句容人也。

translations.literal: Li Nan, courtesy name Xiaoshan, was a native of Jurong in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nan, styled Xiaoshan, came from Jurong in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，明於風角。

translations.literal: In his youth he was devoted to learning and clear-sighted in wind-angle divination.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard in youth and mastered the wind-angle art.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元中，太守馬棱坐盜賊事被徵，當詣廷尉，吏民不寧，南特通謁賀。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era of Emperor He, Governor Ma Ling was impeached on account of bandit affairs and summoned to appear before the minister of justice; clerks and commoners were uneasy, yet Nan alone gained entry to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor He, when Governor Ma Ling was called to the capital on a banditry charge, the commandery panicked—only Li Nan asked for an audience to congratulate him.

sentences.zh: 棱意有恨，謂曰：「太守不德，今當即罪，而君反相賀邪？

translations.literal: Ling harbored resentment and said to him, 'The governor lacks virtue and is now about to be punished—why do you instead congratulate me?'
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ling took offense and said, 'I am disgraced—why do you offer joy?'

sentences.zh: 」南曰：「旦有善風，明日中時，應有吉問，故來稱慶。

translations.literal: ' Nan said, 'This morning there was an auspicious wind; by midday tomorrow there ought to be welcome news, and therefore I have come to speak felicitation.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Nan replied, 'The wind at dawn was favorable; by noon tomorrow good word will arrive—that is why I came to rejoice.'

sentences.zh: 」旦日，棱延望景晏，以為無徵；

translations.literal: ' The next morning Ling waited until the sun stood high, thinking there was no verification;
translations.idiomatic: Next morning Ma Ling watched the sky until noon and saw no sign;

sentences.zh: 至晡，乃有驛使齎詔書原停棱事。

translations.literal: by late afternoon, then, there was a relay courier bearing an edict pardoning and halting proceedings against Ling.
translations.idiomatic: only in mid-afternoon did a post rider gallop up with an edict dropping the case.

sentences.zh: 南問其遲留之狀。

translations.literal: Nan asked about the circumstances of his delay.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nan asked why he was late.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「向度宛陵浦裡斻，馬踠足，是以不得速。

translations.literal: The messenger said, 'Just now when crossing the Wanling inlet at Puli, my horse sprained its foot, and therefore I could not be swift.'
translations.idiomatic: The courier said his horse had stumbled crossing the ford at Wanling, which slowed him down.

sentences.zh: 」棱乃服焉。

translations.literal: ' Ling thereupon submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ling conceded Li Nan had been right.

sentences.zh: 後舉有道，辟公府，病不行，終於家。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended as a man of the Way, summoned to the duke's offices, but pleaded illness and did not go; he ended his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for the 'conduct of the Way' and called to the high minister's bureau, he pleaded sickness and stayed home until he died.

sentences.zh: 南女亦曉家術，為由拳縣人妻。

translations.literal: Nan's daughter also understood the family's arts; she was wife to a man of Youquan county.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nan's daughter knew the family divinations; she had married into Youquan county.

sentences.zh: 晨詣爨室，卒有暴風，婦便上堂從姑求歸，辭其二親。

translations.literal: One morning when she went to the cook-shed, suddenly a violent wind sprang up; the woman at once went up to the hall and begged her mother-in-law to let her return home, taking leave of both parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: One dawn at the kitchen a gale struck; she ran to the hall and begged leave to go home to her parents.

sentences.zh: 姑不許，乃跪而泣曰：「家世傳術，疾風卒起，先吹灶突及井，此禍為婦女主爨者，妾將亡之應。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law would not permit it, so kneeling she wept and said, 'Our house has handed down these arts for generations: when a fierce wind rises suddenly, if it first strikes the stove-flue and the well, this portends calamity for the woman who tends the cook-fires—your handmaid is about to die, and this is the sign.'
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law refused; kneeling, she wept, 'Our family reads omens: a sudden gale that hits the chimney and well first marks the cook's doom—I am the one who will die.'

sentences.zh: 」因著其亡日。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon she wrote down the day of her death.
translations.idiomatic: She named the very day she would die.

sentences.zh: 乃聽還家，如期病卒。

translations.literal: They then let her return home, and on the appointed day she indeed died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: They sent her home, and she fell ill and died exactly as she foretold.

sentences.zh: 李郃字孟節，漢中南鄭人也。

translations.literal: Li He, courtesy name Mengjie, was a native of Nanzheng in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li He, styled Mengjie, came from Nanzheng in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 父頡，以儒學稱，官至博士。

translations.literal: His father Jie was famed for Confucian learning and rose to the rank of academician.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Jie was a noted classicist who reached the doctorate.

sentences.zh: 郃襲父業，游太學，通《五經》。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's occupation, traveled to the Imperial Academy, and mastered the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father's scholarship, entered the Imperial Academy, and mastered the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 善《河》、《洛》風星，外質樸，人莫之識。

translations.literal: He was skilled in River and Luo lore and wind and stars; outwardly he was plain, and no one recognized his worth.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the River-Luo charts and stellar winds, yet seemed so plain that nobody noticed him.

sentences.zh: 縣召署幕門候吏。

translations.literal: The county summoned him and appointed him gate watchman at the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The county put him on duty as watchman at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 和帝即位，分遣使者，皆微服單行，各至州縣，觀采風謠。

translations.literal: When Emperor He took the throne, he separately dispatched envoys, all in plain dress traveling alone, each to commanderies and counties to observe and gather popular songs and sayings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He sent secret inspectors in plain clothes, each riding alone to hear folk songs and rumor.

sentences.zh: 使者二人當到益部，投郃候舍。

translations.literal: Two envoys were to reach Yi province and lodged at He's watch station.
translations.idiomatic: Two of them were bound for Yi and put up at Li He's guardhouse.

sentences.zh: 時，夏夕露坐，郃因仰觀，問曰：「二君發京師時，寧知朝廷遣二使邪？

translations.literal: At the time, on a summer evening sitting in the dew, He therefore looked up at the sky and asked, 'When you two gentlemen set out from the capital, did you know the court had dispatched two envoys?'
translations.idiomatic: One summer night they sat outside; Li He studied the stars and asked whether they knew the court had sent two men like them.

sentences.zh: 」二人默然，驚相視曰：「不聞也。

translations.literal: ' The two were silent, then looked at each other in alarm and said, 'We did not hear of it.'
translations.idiomatic: They stared at each other and said they had heard nothing.

sentences.zh: 」問何以知之。

translations.literal: ' They asked how he knew.
translations.idiomatic: They asked how he could tell.

sentences.zh: 郃指星示云：「有二使星向益州分野，故知之耳。」

translations.literal: He pointed at the stars and showed them, saying, 'There are two envoy-stars moving toward the field division of Yi province—therefore I knew it.'
translations.idiomatic: He traced two 'envoy' stars sliding toward Yi's celestial field—that was his proof.

sentences.zh: 後三年，其使者一人拜漢中太守，郃猶為吏。

translations.literal: After three years, one of those envoys was appointed governor of Hanzhong, and He still served as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later one of those men became governor of Hanzhong while Li He remained a petty clerk.

sentences.zh: 太守奇其隱德，召署戶曹史。

translations.literal: The governor marveled at his hidden virtue and summoned him to serve as clerk of the households bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The new governor, struck by his quiet gifts, made him clerk of the households bureau.

sentences.zh: 時，大將軍竇憲納妻，天下郡國皆有禮慶，郡亦遣使。

translations.literal: At the time the great general Dou Xian took a wife, and every commandery and kingdom in the realm sent congratulatory gifts; the commandery too dispatched an envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Xian married, every province sent gifts; Hanzhong prepared a messenger too.

sentences.zh: 郃進諫曰：「竇將軍椒房之親，不修禮德，而專權驕恣，危亡之禍可翹足而待。

translations.literal: He remonstrated, saying, 'General Dou is kin by marriage to the inner palace, yet he does not cultivate ritual virtue; instead he monopolizes power and acts with arrogant license—the calamity of peril and ruin can be awaited by standing on tiptoe.'
translations.idiomatic: Li He warned, 'Dou Xian is imperial in-law yet flouts virtue and bullies the realm—his fall is a toe's length away.'

sentences.zh: 願明府一心王室，勿與交通。

translations.literal: I beg my enlightened lord to give his whole heart to the royal house and have no dealings with him.'
translations.idiomatic: He begged the governor to cleave to the throne and send no gift.'

sentences.zh: 」太守固遣之，郃不能止。

translations.literal: ' The governor insisted on sending the envoy; He could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: The governor insisted; Li He could not block him.

sentences.zh: 請求自行，許之。

translations.literal: He requested to go in his own person, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to carry the gift himself and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 郃遂所在留遲，以觀其變。

translations.literal: He thereupon lingered wherever he went, to observe how events would turn.
translations.idiomatic: He dawdled at every stop to see what would happen.

sentences.zh: 行至扶風，而憲就國自殺，支黨悉伏其誅。

translations.literal: When he reached Fufeng, Xian went to his fief and killed himself, and his whole faction suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Fufeng, Dou Xian had been sent to his fief and forced to suicide; his clique was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 凡交通憲者，皆為免官，唯漢中太守不豫焉。

translations.literal: In general, all who had dealings with Xian were dismissed from office, but the governor of Hanzhong alone was not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who had courted Dou Xian lost his post—except the Hanzhong governor.

sentences.zh: 郃歲中舉孝廉，五遷尚書令，又拜太常。

translations.literal: Within the year He was recommended as filial and incorrupt, rose through five transfers to director of the secretariat, and was again appointed minister of cults.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Li He won filial-incorrupt rank, climbed five steps to director of the secretariat, then became minister of cults.

sentences.zh: 元初四年，代袁敞為司空，數陳得失，有忠臣節。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanchu he replaced Yuan Chang as minister of works, repeatedly setting forth gain and loss with the integrity of a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanchu 4 he succeeded Yuan Chang as minister of works and spoke bluntly on policy like a true loyalist.

sentences.zh: 在位四年，坐請託事免。

translations.literal: After four years in office he was dismissed for a case of improper solicitation.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he fell on a favor-seeking charge.

sentences.zh: 安帝崩，北鄉侯立，復為司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor An died and the Marquis of Beixiang was enthroned, he again became minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor An died and the Beixiang marquis mounted the throne, Li He returned as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 及北鄉侯病，郃陰與少府河南陶範、步兵校尉趙直謀立順帝，會孫程等事先成，故郃功不顯。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Beixiang fell ill, He secretly plotted with Privy Treasurer Tao Fan of Henan and Colonel of Foot Zhao Zhi to establish Emperor Shun, but Sun Cheng and his party acted first, and therefore He's merit did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy emperor sickened, Li He conspired with Tao Fan and Zhao Zhi to enthrone Emperor Shun, but eunuch Sun Cheng moved first, so his plot never surfaced.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐吏民疾病，仍有災異，賜策免。

translations.literal: The next year, on account of sickness among clerks and people and repeated calamities and prodigies, he was dismissed with a written admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Next year plague and omens cost him his seal under an imperial rebuke.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠翟酺上郃「潛圖大計，以安社稷」，於是錄陰謀之功，封郃涉都侯，辭讓不受。

translations.literal: The master of works Zhai Pu memorialized that He 'secretly framed a great plan to secure the altars of soil and grain,' and therefore his merit in the hidden plot was recorded and He was enfeoffed marquis of Shedu, but he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Pu then praised his hidden role in enthroning Shun; the court offered a marquisate, which Li He refused.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘，卒於家。

translations.literal: At more than eighty years of age he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 門人上黨馮冑獨制服，心喪三年，時人異之。

translations.literal: His disciple Feng Zhou of Shangdang alone wore mourning garb and observed heart-mourning for three years; people of the time marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Only his pupil Feng Zhou of Shangdang wore mourning three years—an act the age found remarkable.

sentences.zh: 冑字世威，奉世之後也。

translations.literal: Zhou, courtesy name Shiwei, was a descendant of Feng Shishi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zhou, styled Shiwei, descended from Feng Shishi.

sentences.zh: 常慕周伯況、閔仲叔之為人，隱處山澤，不應徵辟。

translations.literal: He always admired the conduct of Zhou Bokuang and Min Zhongshu, hiding in mountains and marshes and not answering summons.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled himself on Zhou Bokuang and Min Zhongshu, living hidden in the hills and ignoring every call to office.

sentences.zh: 郃子固，已見前傳。

translations.literal: He's son Gu has already been seen in an earlier biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Gu appears in an earlier chapter.

sentences.zh: 弟子歷，字季子。

translations.literal: His disciple Li, courtesy name Jizi.
translations.idiomatic: A disciple, Li, styled Jizi.

sentences.zh: 清白有節，博學善交，與鄭玄、陳紀等相結。

translations.literal: He was pure, white-handed, and principled, broadly learned and skilled at friendship, and formed ties with Zheng Xuan, Chen Ji, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was incorrupt, learned, and befriended men like Zheng Xuan and Chen Ji.

sentences.zh: 為新城長，政貴無為。

translations.literal: He became magistrate of Xincheng, valuing non-action in government.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Xincheng he ruled by doing little.

sentences.zh: 亦好方術。

translations.literal: He also loved occult arts.
translations.idiomatic: He too dabbled in esoteric technique.

sentences.zh: 時，天下旱，縣界特雨。

translations.literal: At the time the realm suffered drought, but within his county boundaries it rained especially.
translations.idiomatic: While the empire baked in drought, his county alone caught rain.

sentences.zh: 官至奉車都尉。

translations.literal: His office rose to chief commandant of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief commandant for the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 段翳字元章，廣漢新都人也。

translations.literal: Duan Yi, courtesy name Yuanzhang, was a native of Xindu in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yi, styled Yuanzhang, came from Xindu in Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 習《易經》，明風角。

translations.literal: He studied the *Book of Changes* and understood wind-angle divination.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the *Changes* and the wind-angle art.

sentences.zh: 時有就其學者，雖未至，必豫知其姓名。

translations.literal: At the time, when there were those who came to study with him, although they had not yet arrived, he always beforehand knew their names.
translations.idiomatic: Pupils who had not yet arrived found their names already on his lips.

sentences.zh: 嘗告守津吏曰：「某日當有諸生二人，荷擔問翳舍處者，幸為告之。

translations.literal: He once told the ferry-clerk on guard, 'On such-and-such a day there will be two students carrying loads who will ask where Yi's house is—be so good as to tell them.'
translations.idiomatic: He once told a ferry guard that two laden students would ask for him on a set day—please direct them.

sentences.zh: 」後竟如其言。

translations.literal: ' Later it turned out exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: It happened just as he said.

sentences.zh: 又有一生來學，積年，自謂略究要術，辭歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Again there was a student who came to study; after many years he claimed to have roughly grasped the essential arts and took leave to return to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: Another pupil studied years, thought he had the gist, and left for home.

sentences.zh: 翳為合膏藥，並以簡書封於筒中，告生曰：「有急發視之。

translations.literal: Yi compounded an ointment for him, and together with a writing on bamboo slips sealed it in a tube, telling the student, 'If there is an emergency, open and look at it.'
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yi gave him salve and a sealed bamboo slip, saying, 'Open only in crisis.'

sentences.zh: 」生到葭萌，與吏爭度，津吏楇破從者頭。

translations.literal: ' When the student reached Jiameng, he quarreled with a clerk over crossing; the ferry clerk struck with a cudgel and broke the head of his attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiameng he fought the ferryman, who clubbed his servant's head open.

sentences.zh: 生開筒得書，言到葭萌，與吏鬥頭破者，以此膏裹之。

translations.literal: The student opened the tube and obtained the writing, which said that when he reached Jiameng and fought with a clerk so that a head was broken, he should wrap it with this ointment.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the tube the slip said that at Jiameng a clerk would crack someone's skull and this salve would heal it.

sentences.zh: 生用其言，創者即愈。

translations.literal: The student used his words, and the wounded man at once recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the paste and the wound closed overnight.

sentences.zh: 生嘆服，乃還卒業。

translations.literal: The student sighed in submission and returned to finish his studies.
translations.idiomatic: Awestruck, the student went back to finish the course.

sentences.zh: 翳遂隱居竄跡，終於家。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon lived in reclusion, effacing his tracks, and ended his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yi then vanished into reclusion and died at home.

sentences.zh: 廖扶字文起，汝南平輿人也。

translations.literal: Liao Fu, courtesy name Wenqi, was a native of Pingyu in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Fu, styled Wenqi, came from Pingyu in Runan.

sentences.zh: 習《韓詩》、《歐陽尚書》，教授常數百人。

translations.literal: He studied the Han version of the *Odes* and the Ouyang *Documents*, and regularly had several hundred pupils in instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the Han *Odes* and Ouyang *Documents* to hundreds of students.

sentences.zh: 父為北地太守，永初中，坐羌沒郡下獄死。

translations.literal: His father had been governor of Beidi; in the Yongchu era he was imprisoned and died because the Qiang had overrun the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father governed Beidi and died in prison after the Qiang overran the commandery in Yongchu.

sentences.zh: 扶感父以法喪身，憚為吏。

translations.literal: Fu, moved that his father had lost his life through the law, feared to become an official.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Fu shrank from office after seeing the law kill his father.

sentences.zh: 及服終而歎曰：「老子有言：『名與身孰親？

translations.literal: When mourning was ended he sighed, saying, 'Laozi has a saying, "Fame and the person—which is dearer?"'
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he quoted Laozi—fame or life, which matters more?

sentences.zh: 』吾豈為名乎！

translations.literal: ' How could I do it for the sake of fame!'
translations.idiomatic: Surely I will not chase reputation!'

sentences.zh: 」遂絕志世外。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he cut off ambition for the world beyond.
translations.idiomatic: He renounced the world of ambition.

sentences.zh: 專精經典，尤明天文、讖緯，風角、推步之術。

translations.literal: He concentrated on the classics, being especially clear on astronomy, chenwei apocrypha, wind-angle, and calendrical reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He plunged into the canon, mastering stars, apocrypha, wind-angle, and calendars.

sentences.zh: 州郡公府辟召，皆不應。

translations.literal: Summons from provincial commandery and ducal offices he would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored every summons from province or capital.

sentences.zh: 就問災異，亦無所對。

translations.literal: When they came to ask about calamities and prodigies, he likewise made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Even when asked for omens he stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 扶逆知歲荒，乃聚谷數千斛，悉用給宗族姻親，又斂葬遭疫死亡不能自收者。

translations.literal: Fu foreknew years of famine; he therefore gathered several thousand hu of grain and used it all to supply kinsmen and affines, and also gathered for burial those who had died of plague and could not bury themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing famine, he stored grain for clan and in-laws and buried plague victims who had no one to tend them.

sentences.zh: 常居先人塚側，未曾入城市。

translations.literal: He constantly dwelt beside his ancestors' tombs and never entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He lived by the family graves and never went to town.

sentences.zh: 太守謁煥，先為諸生，從扶學。

translations.literal: Governor Ye Huan had formerly been a student and studied under Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ye Huan had once been his pupil.

sentences.zh: 後臨郡，未到，先遣吏修門人之禮，又欲擢扶子弟，固不肯，當時人因號為北郭先生。

translations.literal: Later, when he came to govern the commandery, before arriving he first sent a clerk to perform the rites of a disciple, and also wished to promote Fu's sons and younger brothers, but Fu firmly refused; people of the time therefore styled him Master North of the Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Huan, before taking his post, sent a man to honor him as teacher and tried to promote his sons; Liao Fu refused and was nicknamed the Sage beyond the north wall.

sentences.zh: 年八十，終於家。

translations.literal: At eighty years of age he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at eighty.

sentences.zh: 二子，孟舉、偉舉，並知名。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Mengju and Weiju, both of whom became known.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Mengju and Weiju both won renown.

sentences.zh: 折像字伯式，廣漢雒人也。

translations.literal: She Xiang, courtesy name Boshi, was a native of Luo in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: She Xiang, styled Boshi, came from Luo in Guanghan.
