sentences.zh: 其先張江者，封折侯，曾孫國為鬱林太守，徙廣漢，因封氏焉。

translations.literal: His ancestor Zhang Jiang had been enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhe; a great-grandson's state became governor of Yulin and moved to Guanghan, whereupon they took the clan name from the fief.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor, Zhang Jiang, was marquis of Zhe; a descendant governed Yulin, moved to Guanghan, and adopted the fief name She as surname.

sentences.zh: 國生像。

translations.literal: Guo sired Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: She Guo fathered She Xiang.

sentences.zh: 國有資財二億，家僮八百人。

translations.literal: Guo had property worth two hundred million cash and eight hundred household retainers.
translations.idiomatic: She Guo owned two hundred million cash and eight hundred retainers.

sentences.zh: 像幼有仁心，不殺昆蟲，不折萌牙。

translations.literal: Xiang in his youth had a benevolent heart: he did not kill insects and did not break off tender shoots.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy She Xiang spared insects and never snapped young shoots.

sentences.zh: 能通《京氏易》，好黃、老言。

translations.literal: He could penetrate the Jing family's *Changes* and loved the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Jing Fang's *Changes* and loved Huang-Lao philosophy.

sentences.zh: 及國卒，感多藏厚亡之義，乃散金帛資產，周施親疏。

translations.literal: When Guo died, moved by the meaning that 'much hoarding means a thick loss,' he scattered gold, silk, and assets, distributing them to kin whether close or distant.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he remembered that great hoards invite great loss and gave away gold, silk, and land to kin near and far.

sentences.zh: 或諫像曰：「君三男兩女，孫息盈前，當增益產業，何為坐自殫竭乎？

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated with Xiang, saying, 'You have three sons and two daughters, and grandchildren throng before you—you ought to increase your estate; why sit and exhaust yourself?'
translations.idiomatic: Friends urged him to keep the fortune for three sons, two daughters, and a brood of grandchildren.

sentences.zh: 」像曰：「昔斗子文有言：『我乃逃禍，非避富也。

translations.literal: ' Xiang said, 'Formerly Dou Ziwen said, "I am thereby escaping calamity, not fleeing wealth."'
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Dou Ziwen: 'I shed wealth to dodge disaster, not because I scorn riches.'

sentences.zh: 』吾門戶殖財日久，盈滿之咎，道家所忌。

translations.literal: ' My gate has piled up wealth a long time; the blame of overflowing fullness is what the Daoist teaching forbids.
translations.idiomatic: Our house has been rich too long; Daoists warn that excess invites ruin.

sentences.zh: 今世將衰，子又不才。

translations.literal: The present generation is about to decline, and my sons moreover lack talent.
translations.idiomatic: The age is turning and my sons lack talent.

sentences.zh: 不仁而富，謂之不幸。

translations.literal: To be without benevolence yet rich is called misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth without virtue is the worst misfortune.

sentences.zh: 牆隙而高，其崩必疾也。

translations.literal: A wall cracked yet built high—its collapse must be swift.'
translations.idiomatic: A high wall built on a crack must fall fast.'

sentences.zh: 」智者聞之，咸服焉。

translations.literal: ' When wise men heard this, they all submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful listeners took his point and conceded he was right.

sentences.zh: 自知亡日，召賓客九族飲食辭訣，忽然而終。

translations.literal: Knowing beforehand the day of his death, he summoned guests and the nine degrees of kin for food and drink and farewell words, then suddenly passed away.
translations.idiomatic: He foreknew his last day, feasted kin and friends in farewell, and slipped away as if in a breath.

sentences.zh: 時年八十四。

translations.literal: At the time he was eighty-four sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 家無餘資，諸子衰劣如其言云。

translations.literal: The household had no surplus resources, and his sons proved feeble and inferior, just as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: The estate was bare, and his sons turned out as dull as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 樊英字季齊，南陽魯陽人也。

translations.literal: Fan Ying, courtesy name Jiqi, was a native of Luyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying, styled Jiqi, came from Luyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 少受業三輔，習《京氏易》，兼明《五經》。

translations.literal: In his youth he received instruction in the Three Adjuncts region, studied the Jing family's *Changes*, and was conversant with the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in the capital region, mastered Jing Fang's *Changes*, and knew the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 又善風角、星算，《河》、《洛》七緯，推步災異。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in wind-angle, star reckoning, the River and Luo texts and the seven weft-books, and calendrical inference of calamities and prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: He read wind omens, stars, River-Luo lore, the seven weft apocrypha, and disaster math.

sentences.zh: 隱於壺山之陽，受業者四方而至。

translations.literal: He hid on the south slope of Mount Hu, and those who came to study with him arrived from the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He lived south of Mount Hu and drew pupils from every direction.

sentences.zh: 州郡前後禮請，不應；

translations.literal: The province and commandery repeatedly paid him ritual respect and invited him, but he would not respond;
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery posts courted him in vain;

sentences.zh: 公卿舉賢良方正、有道，皆不行。

translations.literal: the dukes and ministers recommended him as worthy, good, and upright, and as a man of the Way, but in every case he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: high ministers nominated him as worthy and as a man of the Way, yet he never took office.

sentences.zh: 嘗有暴風從西方起，英謂學者曰：「成都市火甚盛。

translations.literal: Once a violent wind rose from the west; Ying said to his students, 'In Chengdu market the fire is very fierce.'
translations.idiomatic: When a gale blew from the west he told his class, 'Chengdu's market is burning hard.'

sentences.zh: 」因含水西向漱之，乃令記其日時。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he held water in his mouth and spat it toward the west, then ordered them to record the day and hour.
translations.idiomatic: He rinsed his mouth westward with water and had them note the time.

sentences.zh: 客後有從蜀都來，云「是日大火，有黑雲卒從東起，須臾大雨，火遂得滅。

translations.literal: ' Later a guest came from Shu capital and said, 'That day there was a great fire; suddenly a black cloud rose from the east, and in a moment there was heavy rain, so the fire was then able to be extinguished.'
translations.idiomatic: A traveler from Shu reported a great blaze that day, then black clouds from the east and a downpour that snuffed the flames.

sentences.zh: 」於是天下稱其術藝。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon the realm praised his arts.
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven marveled at his skill.

sentences.zh: 永建二年，順帝策書備禮，玄纁徵之，复固辭疾篤。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongjian, Emperor Shun, with a written summons and full ritual, summoned him in dark silk and crimson, but again he firmly declined on grounds of grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjian 2 Emperor Shun summoned him with full honors; Fan Ying pleaded grave illness again.

sentences.zh: 乃詔切責郡縣，駕載上道。

translations.literal: An edict then sternly rebuked the commandery and county and ordered him carried in a carriage onto the road.
translations.idiomatic: The court rebuked local officials and had him carted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 英不得已，到京，稱疾不肯起。

translations.literal: Ying had no choice but to reach the capital, where he pleaded illness and refused to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying yielded, arrived, and stayed abed feigning sickness.

sentences.zh: 乃強輿入殿，猶不以禮屈。

translations.literal: They then forced him in a litter into the hall, yet still he would not bend to ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: They carried him into the hall on a litter; he still refused court etiquette.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謂英曰：「朕能生君，能殺君；

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and said to Ying, 'I can give you life, I can kill you;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thundered, 'I can spare or end you;

sentences.zh: 能貴君，能賤君；

translations.literal: I can honor you, I can humble you;
translations.idiomatic: raise you high or cast you low;

sentences.zh: 能富君，能貧君。

translations.literal: I can enrich you, I can impoverish you.
translations.idiomatic: make you rich or strip you bare.'

sentences.zh: 君何以慢朕命？

translations.literal: Why do you slight my command?'
translations.idiomatic: Why defy an emperor?'

sentences.zh: 」英曰：「臣受命於天。

translations.literal: ' Ying said, 'Your servant received his mandate from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying answered, 'My life comes from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 生盡其命，天也；

translations.literal: To live out one's allotted span is Heaven's doing;
translations.idiomatic: Live your full span—that is Heaven;

sentences.zh: 死不得其命，亦天也。

translations.literal: to die without obtaining one's allotted span is also Heaven's doing.
translations.idiomatic: die before your time—that too is Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 陛下焉能生臣，焉能殺臣！

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty give your servant life, how can Your Majesty kill your servant!
translations.idiomatic: So how can you grant me life or deal me death?'

sentences.zh: 臣見暴君如見仇讎，立其朝猶不肯，可得而貴乎？

translations.literal: Your servant sees a cruel lord as he would a foe; to stand in his court your servant would still refuse—can he then be honored?
translations.idiomatic: I would sooner face a tyrant as an enemy than bow in his court—can you truly honor me?'

sentences.zh: 雖在布衣之列，環堵之中，晏然自得，不易萬乘之尊，又可得而賤乎？

translations.literal: Although among the ranks of common cloth, within a ring of earthen walls, he is calmly self-contented and would not exchange the honor of the ten thousand chariots—can he then be humbled?
translations.idiomatic: Give me a hovel and plain clothes and I am content—I would not swap that for the throne—can you humble me?'

sentences.zh: 陛下焉能貴臣，焉能賤臣！

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty honor your servant, how can Your Majesty humble your servant!
translations.idiomatic: So how can you honor or shame me?'

sentences.zh: 臣非禮之祿，雖萬鍾不受；

translations.literal: Your servant will not accept salary that is not in accord with ritual, though it be ten thousand zhong;
translations.idiomatic: Unrighteous stipends, even ten thousand zhong, I reject;

sentences.zh: 若申其志，雖簞食不厭也。

translations.literal: if his aims are declared, though it be basket-gruel he does not weary of it.
translations.idiomatic: feed my purpose and a bowl of gruel satisfies me.'

sentences.zh: 陛下焉能富臣，焉能貧臣！

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty enrich your servant, how can Your Majesty impoverish your servant!'
translations.idiomatic: So how can you enrich or ruin me?'

sentences.zh: 」帝不能屈，而敬其名，使出就太醫養疾，月致羊、酒。

translations.literal: ' The emperor could not bend him, but respected his name, ordered him out to convalesce under the grand physician, and each month sent sheep and wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not break him, yet prized his name, sent him to the imperial physicians, and monthly supplied mutton and wine.

sentences.zh: 至四年三月，天子乃為英設壇席，令公車令導，尚書奉引，賜几杖，待以師傅之禮，延問得失。

translations.literal: By the third month of the fourth year, the Son of Heaven then for Ying set up an altar and mats, ordered the director of the imperial coaches to conduct him, the secretariat to lead him in, bestowed a bench and staff, treated him with the rites due a tutor, and extended inquiry into gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year the emperor staged a dais for Fan Ying, had coaches and secretaries escort him, gave him a seat and cane, honored him like a teacher, and asked his counsel on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 英不敢辭，拜五官中郎將。

translations.literal: Ying did not dare refuse, and was appointed supernumerary gentleman of the household.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying bowed and accepted rank as supernumerary gentleman of the household.

sentences.zh: 數月，英稱疾篤，詔以為光祿大夫，賜告歸。

translations.literal: After several months Ying pleaded grave illness; an edict made him grand counselor of the palace and granted him leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he pleaded worse health; the court named him grand counselor of the palace and let him go home.

sentences.zh: 令在所送谷千斛，常以八月致牛一頭，酒三斛；

translations.literal: It ordered the place where he dwelt to send a thousand hu of grain, and regularly in the eighth month to deliver one head of ox and three hu of wine;
translations.idiomatic: His district was told to send a thousand hu of grain yearly, each eighth month an ox and three hu of wine;

sentences.zh: 如有不幸，祠以中牢。

translations.literal: if misfortune should befall him, to sacrifice with the middle victim.
translations.idiomatic: and if he died, to sacrifice with the middle offering.

sentences.zh: 英辭位不受，有詔譬旨，勿聽。

translations.literal: Ying declined the office and would not accept; there was an edict explaining the intent and ordering him not to be heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to refuse the title; the emperor insisted he keep it.

sentences.zh: 英初被詔命，僉以為必不降志，及後應對，又無奇謨深策，談者以為失望。

translations.literal: When Ying first received the summons, all thought he would surely not lower his resolve, but when afterward he answered and conversed, he had no marvelous stratagems or deep plans, and those who discussed it thought themselves disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: At first everyone expected Fan Ying to defy the throne; when he took office without brilliant policy, chatter called him a letdown.

sentences.zh: 初，河南張楷與英俱徵，既而謂英曰：「天下有二道，出與處也。

translations.literal: At first Zhang Kai of Henan had been summoned together with Ying; afterward he said to Ying, 'Under heaven there are two paths—going out and staying in.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's Zhang Kai, summoned with him, later said, 'There are two paths—serve or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 吾前以子之出，能輔是君也，濟斯人也。

translations.literal: I formerly thought that in your going out you would be able to assist this lord and succor these people.
translations.idiomatic: I thought you went to aid the ruler and save the people.

sentences.zh: 而子始以不訾之身，怒萬乘之主；

translations.literal: Yet you began with a body beyond price and angered the lord of ten thousand chariots;
translations.idiomatic: Instead you, a man beyond price, first enraged the Son of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 及其享受爵祿，又不聞匡救之術，進退無所據矣。」

translations.literal: when it came to your enjoying rank and stipend, one did not hear arts of correction and rescue—there is no footing for advance or retreat.'
translations.idiomatic: then took salary without offering bold counsel—your stance makes no sense.'

sentences.zh: 英既善術，朝廷每有災異，詔輒下問變復之效，所言多驗。

translations.literal: Ying was indeed skilled in technique; whenever the court had calamities or prodigies, edicts regularly went down asking the efficacy of restoration through change, and what he said was mostly verified.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying's arts were real: whenever omens struck, the court asked him how to set the cosmos right, and he was usually right.

sentences.zh: 初，英著《易章句》，世名樊氏學，以圖緯教授。

translations.literal: At first Ying composed *Explanatory Sentences on the Changes*, known in the age as the Fan school, and taught by charts and weft-texts.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote *Fan's Commentary on the Changes* and taught with charts and apocrypha.

sentences.zh: 潁川陳寔，少從英學。

translations.literal: Chen Shi of Yingchuan in his youth studied under Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi of Yingchuan studied under him as a boy.

sentences.zh: 嘗有疾，妻遣婢拜問，英下床答拜。

translations.literal: Once when Ying was ill, his wife sent a maid to bow and inquire; Ying got down from the bed and returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: Once ill, he rose from bed to return a maid's courtesy sent by Chen Shi's wife.

sentences.zh: 寔怪而問之。

translations.literal: Shi marveled and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi asked why.

sentences.zh: 英曰：「妻，齊也。

translations.literal: Ying said, 'The wife is one's equal.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying said, 'A wife is partner, not servant.'

sentences.zh: 共奉祭祀，禮無不答。

translations.literal: Together they perform the sacrifices; in ritual there is none whom one does not answer.'
translations.idiomatic: We share the ancestral rites—propriety demands I answer her messenger.'

sentences.zh: 」其恭謹若是。

translations.literal: ' Such was his reverent care.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his punctilious courtesy.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，卒於家。

translations.literal: At more than seventy sui he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 孫陵，靈帝時以諂事宦人為司徒。

translations.literal: Sun Ling, in the time of Emperor Ling, by fawning on the eunuchs became minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ling flattered the palace eunuchs under Emperor Ling and rose to minister of education.

sentences.zh: 陳郡郤巡，學傳英業，官至侍中。

translations.literal: Xi Xun of Chen commandery studied and transmitted Ying's occupation and rose to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xun of Chen carried on Fan Ying's teaching and reached palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 論曰：漢世之所謂名士者，其風流可知矣。

translations.literal: The judgment says: As for those whom the Han age called 'eminent gentlemen,' their style and current may be known.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: the Han fashion for 'famous scholars' tells its own tale.

sentences.zh: 雖弛張趣舍，時有未純，於刻情修容，依倚道藝，以就其聲價，非所能通物方，弘時務也。

translations.literal: Although in tension and relaxation, taking and leaving office, they were at times not pure, in carving emotion and cultivating appearance, leaning on the Way and its arts to build reputation and price, they were not those who could comprehend things in the round or enlarge the business of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Some tightened or loosened their principles, trimmed their manners, and traded on technique for fame, yet few could grasp the world or serve the times.

sentences.zh: 及徵樊英、楊厚，朝廷若待神明，至，竟無他異。

translations.literal: When Fan Ying and Yang Hou were summoned, the court treated them as spirits—yet when they arrived there was in the end nothing else extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying and Yang Hou were awaited like gods; when they came they offered no marvels.

sentences.zh: 英名最高，毀最甚。

translations.literal: Ying's name was highest, and the slander against him was worst.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying's reputation stood tallest—and drew the bitterest mockery.

sentences.zh: 李固、硃穆等，以為處士純盜虛名，無益於用，故其所以然也。

translations.literal: Li Gu, Zhu Mu, and others held that recluses were pure thieves of empty fame, of no benefit to use—hence it was so.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu and Zhu Mu judged such hermits mere hoarders of hollow renown, useless on the job—and so it looked.

sentences.zh: 然而後進希之以成名，世主禮之以得眾，原其無用亦所以為用，則其有用或歸於無用矣。

translations.literal: Yet later students hoped through them to make a name, and worldly lords honored them to win the multitude; tracing their uselessness, it thereby became their usefulness, so that their usefulness might in turn revert to uselessness.
translations.idiomatic: Still, juniors aped them for renown and rulers courted them for crowds; their very uselessness became a political tool, until usefulness and uselessness traded places.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How shall we speak of it?
translations.idiomatic: How shall we put this?

sentences.zh: 夫煥乎文章，時或乖用；

translations.literal: Splendid indeed is literary pattern—yet the times may misuse it;
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant writing can still be misapplied;

sentences.zh: 本乎禮樂，適末或疏。

translations.literal: rooted in ritual and music, toward the branch tips one may sometimes grow negligent.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and music anchor the root, yet the twigs may run wild.

sentences.zh: 及其陶搢紳，藻心性，使由之而不知者，豈非道邈用表，乖之數跡乎？

translations.literal: When it comes to molding the gentry and polishing the nature of the heart so that they follow it without knowing—can this not be because the Way is remote and its application superficial, a matter of missing the mark by a hair's breadth?
translations.idiomatic: When doctrine refines the elite yet they follow blindly, has not the Way grown so thin its use is only veneer—a hair's miss from the mark?

sentences.zh: 而或者忽不踐之地，賒無用之功，至乃誚噪遠術，賤斥國華，以為力詐可以救淪敝，文律足以致寧平，智盡於猜察，道足於法令，雖濟萬世，其將與夷狄同也。

translations.literal: Yet some tread ground they should not, pursue merit that is of no use, until they sneer at distant arts and cheapen the flower of the state, thinking force and cunning can save a sinking age, that statutes alone can bring peace, that wisdom exhausts itself in suspicion, that the Way stops at laws and orders—even if it succors ten thousand generations, they will end the same as the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Worse are those who scorn high learning, mock statecraft, and trust only force, statutes, and suspicion—such men may save a day but will civilize no better than barbarians.

sentences.zh: 孟軻有言曰：「以夏變夷，不聞變夷於夏。

translations.literal: Meng Ke has a saying: 'Use the Xia to change the Yi; I have not heard of changing the Xia by the Yi.'
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, 'Use civilization to transform barbarism, not the reverse.'

sentences.zh: 」況有未濟者乎！

translations.literal: ' How much more when the work is not yet completed!
translations.idiomatic: —and how much less when the task is unfinished!'
